failures.title: BMW N47T Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure - 2010-2014 models
items.whatHappens: The rear-mounted timing chain and its plastic guides are prone to premature stretch and snapping. This often presents as a metallic rattling noise from the back of the engine on cold starts. If ignored, the chain can snap, causing catastrophic valve and piston damage.
items.repairVsReplace: While a standalone chain kit replacement costs £650-£1,800, the labour-intensive access means that if the engine has already suffered internal damage, a full BMW N47T engine replacement is often the only viable route. Read our full timing chain failure guide.

items.title: Turbocharger and EGR/DPF Clogging - Urban driving profiles
items.whatHappens: The variable geometry turbocharger vanes can stick due to carbon buildup, leading to a loss of power and limp mode. This is frequently compounded by EGR valve and DPF clogging, especially in vehicles used primarily for short, urban journeys.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo cleaning or replacement (£1,200-£2,500) can resolve the issue if caught early. However, if turbo failure has sent debris into the intercooler or engine, a full unit replacement is required to prevent immediate repeat failure.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2011 N47T units received revised tensioners and updated chain guides, making catastrophic failures less frequent than in the pre-2010 non-TU variants, though the fundamental rear-chain design vulnerability remains .
failures.cta: → Compare rebuilt BMW N47T engine prices with the failure already addressed

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the N47T
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The N47T (often designated internally by BMW as N47TU, N47D20O1, or N47D20C) can be identified by the engine code stamped on the block, visible on your V5C registration document, or via a VIN decoder. It is most commonly confused with the earlier non-TU N47D20A or N47D20B, and the newer B47D20A. Fitting the wrong revision can lead to ECU mapping mismatches, incorrect turbo plumbing, and mounting point discrepancies.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement BMW N47T - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used BMW N47T is only advisable for lower-value host vehicles and must come with documented proof that the timing chain assembly was replaced before the 80,000-mile mark. Without this history, the risk of inheriting the same premature failure is high. Explore our vetted used engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the N47T. A proper reconditioning process will replace the notorious rear timing chain, tensioners, guides, and turbocharger seals, directly addressing the engine's most common failure points while restoring factory compression. View reconditioned BMW N47T options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the host vehicle is a higher-mileage 5 Series or X3 where long-term ownership is planned. An upgraded rebuild should include a reinforced timing chain kit, updated oil pump, and a remapped ECU to ensure longevity. Compare rebuilt BMW N47T specialists.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Choosing a supply-and-fit service through our network ensures the engine is installed by a specialist familiar with the N47T's rear-chain access challenges, backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The N47T is typically found in vehicles valued between £3,000 and £9,000. Because a full reconditioned replacement can cost upwards of £3,850 fitted, the replacement cost can approach or exceed 50% of the vehicle's value on older examples. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW N47T engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned BMW N47T engine typically costs between £3,200 and £5,500 for supply only, or £3,850 to £6,410 fully fitted by an independent specialist . Used units start around £1,800 but carry a high risk without documented chain history. Rebuilt units (£4,500-£6,500) include comprehensive upgrades to known weak points. Labour typically adds £650-£910 due to rear-chain access complexity.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure with the BMW N47T engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dominant failure is premature timing chain stretch and tensioner failure, typically occurring between 60,000 and 120,000 miles. The rear-mounted chain design makes access labour-intensive, often presenting as a metallic rattle on cold starts. If ignored, the chain can snap, causing catastrophic valve and piston damage. A proper reconditioned unit will systematically include an updated chain kit and tensioner.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW models use the N47T engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW N47T was widely fitted to the 1 Series (F20/F21), 3 Series (E90/E91 LCI and F30/F31), 5 Series (F10/F11), X1 (E84), and X3 (F25) between 2010 and 2014. It powers various badges including the 116d, 118d, 120d, 318d, 320d, 520d, and xDrive20d. Power outputs range from 116 hp to 184 hp depending on the specific tune. Always verify your exact fitment using your registration number.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned BMW N47T engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned BMW N47T is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of inherited timing chain and turbocharger wear. Used engines (£1,800-£3,200) are only viable if they come with documented proof of a recent timing chain replacement. Reconditioned units (£3,200-£5,500) systematically replace the chain, guides, tensioners, and seals, offering a 12- to 24-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the N47T engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document (Section D.2), the physical stamp on the engine block, or by entering your registration number above. The N47T is often internally designated as N47TU, N47D20O1, or N47D20C. Do not confuse it with the earlier N47D20A/B or the newer B47D20A, as mounting points and ECU mappings differ significantly.
